text:
elsa: Console flagged ~400 invoke_rejects for tool="checkout_hook" on route="payment-canary". Top reasons: "parse_error" and "invalid_output_shape". Anyone?

frank: Sample from logs:
`{"req":"r-5f","tool":"checkout_hook","error":"invalid_output_shape","expected":{"type":"object","fields":["action","details"]},"actual":"{\"action\":\"charge\",\"details\":{\"amt\":100}}"}`

yuan: Looks like model returned a JSON-encoded string instead of object. We recently pushed a token-compact tag; might be the cause. Shouldn't have hit canary though.

elsa: Query: `select count(*) from invokes where route='payment-canary' and reject=true and ts > now()-interval '6 hours'` -> 412 rejects, clustered by a single model tag.

frank: Short-term: adapter can attempt a single JSON parse when actual is string-looking, set `coercion=parse_json_string`, mark `validation_action=coerced` and `soft_reject=true`. Deploy to payment-canary only.

yuan: Agree but TTL the shim to 3 hours and log both original_raw and parsed_payload to S3 (sample 1%). Also add preflight schema check in model push CI: run 30 canonical prompts and assert output_is_object for tools.

telemetry-bot: Proposed tags: validation_reason, validation_action, coercion_detail, route_origin. Sample full payloads at 1% redact PII. Add metric `reject_rate_by_route` and alert if >0.2% for 10m.

elsa: Console UX request: add filter for `validation_action` and show example raw vs coerced payload with a short "how to fix" link (rollback tag / model fix / adapter patch). Support wants quick visibility.

frank: I'll push adapter PR for parse-shim and include trace flag. CI local tests green.

deploy-bot: deploy started: adapter-parse-shim -> payment-canary (initiated by frank) :truck:

telemetry-bot: Billing alerts for validation-rejects suppressed for 30min while we monitor.

frank: Shim live on payment-canary; seeing immediate drop in pages. Will watch coercion_rate and revert model tag if coercion > 0.5% for 15m.

yuan: I'll land the model preflight check tomorrow. Thanks team.
